name: Monotonic Yang Dimension
definition: The **monotonic Yang dimension** is the subfamily-monotonic version of Yang dimension: $$\mathrm{Y}^*(\mathcal{H}) := \max_{\mathcal{G}\subseteq\mathcal{H}} \mathrm{Y}(\mathcal{G}).$$
graph_summary: Maximum Yang dimension over all subfamilies of the class.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.

monotonic.proof: This is immediate from Y*(H)=max_{G subseteq H} Y(G): every subfamily of a subfamily of H is also a subfamily of H.

p_monotonic.proof: For a projection pi(H), every subfamily is the projection of a subfamily of H.  Yang dimension is projection-monotonic, so taking maxima over subfamilies preserves the bound.
